public_rationale: Vectara’s November 1, 2023 results reported hallucinations in 3.0% of GPT-4 summaries and 3.5% of GPT-3.5 Turbo summaries, using an automated model to detect unsupported content when source documents were supplied [e6]. These recurring errors support the interpretation that GPT’s factual outputs required independent checking during the November 1–22 assessment period [e6]. Vectara’s November 6 announcement reported that OpenAI’s models performed best among those tested, but that comparative lead did not eliminate the observed errors [e6, e7].
limitations: The conclusion concerns unchecked factual reliance; the summarization results do not establish that every GPT answer is false or that GPT has no useful applications [e6].
These task-specific rates do not measure factual reliability across all domains or GPT deployments [e6].
The evaluation used an automated hallucination detector, rather than establishing each classification through independent human verification [e6].
